body_html:
Three weeks into a monthly rental you have to fly home for a family event, and you will be away for about three weeks. The bike will sit unused while the rental calendar keeps moving. You have three broad choices: keep the bike parked and the rental running, ask the shop whether the rental can be paused, or return the bike and book again when you are back. Each depends on answers only the shop can give, so the useful move is to compare the options and confirm each one in writing before you leave.

Three options side by side

OptionWhat it means in practiceWhat to confirm
Hold the bikeThe bike stays with you, parked, and the monthly rental continues as agreedWhether the rental is charged for the days you are away, where the bike can be kept and what happens if it is damaged or taken while you are gone
Pause the rentalYou ask the shop to stop the clock for the days abroad, with the bike left at the shop or with youWhether a pause is possible at all, how it is written and how the end date and the next payment move
Return and rebookYou return the bike, close the record and start a new rental when you are backWhether the same bike and rate are available, whether a new deposit entry is needed and what the new start date is

None of the three is something this guide can promise for Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà. All three are worth asking about, ideally a week or more before the flight.

Put numbers beside each option

A simple worksheet turns three vague options into three totals you can compare. For each option write down the cost of the days you are away, any new deposit or fee, the cost of getting a bike again when you return, and the effort involved. For illustration, suppose a monthly rental covers 30 days and you are away for 21 of them. If the shop charges the full month while you are away, 21 of the 30 days, or 70 percent of the period, are paid for and unused.

If the shop agrees to a pause, the days away may not be charged and the end date would move, but how a pause works is for the shop to say. If you return and rebook, ask whether prepaid days are credited or refunded; you also take on a new start date and possibly a different rate.

The figures 30 and 21 are only an example; the real calculation uses the dates and rate the shop confirms.

If you keep the bike parked

  • Choose the place carefully. A building with someone on duty or a locked yard is better than a street. Can You Leave a Rental Motorbike Parked While Travelling Overnight? covers the questions for a single night; three weeks makes them more important.
  • Record the starting state. Photograph every side and the odometer on the day you leave, and note the date.
  • Take out what you do not want to lose from the storage compartment, including a helmet that is yours.
  • Lock it properly. Lock the steering and add a second lock, and ask the shop whether anything should be done about the battery, since a petrol bike left unused can be slow to start.
  • Tell the shop where the bike is, in case it needs to find it while you are away.

If you ask for a pause

Get any agreement in writing before you fly. The message should state the first and last day away, what happens to the rental period in between, whether the bike stays with you or at the shop, and the new end date of the month. A pause that exists only as a spoken "no problem" is easy to remember differently in three weeks. Keep a photograph of the reply with the date visible, and ask the shop to repeat the new end date back to you.

If you return the bike and rebook

Treat the return as a full return: the walk-around, the odometer, the receipt. Returning a Rental Motorbike in Hanoi: A Receipt and Handover Checklist lists what to record, and Hanoi Motorbike Rental Deposits: How to Record Payment and Return covers how to record the payment and the return. Ask whether the same bike can be held for you, whether the rate is the same when you are back and whether a new rental needs the paperwork done again.

A message to send a week before you fly

Put these points in the message:

  • the bike you have and the dates of the monthly rental;
  • the first and last day you will be away;
  • the three options, with a request to say which of them the shop can offer;
  • for each option, what will be charged for the days away, the new end date and what you need to do before you leave;
  • a request for the reply in writing.

Keep the reply with your booking record, and tell the shop at once if your flight dates move, because a changed date needs a second message.

The shop's monthly rental page has rates and booking details for a month or more. The shop's number is 0334 699 969, and it is open 09:00–21:00 daily.
